requirement:
YAML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a mapping value. A `#` within quoted text or
within the content of a block scalar belongs to the scalar.
rationale:
structural: Every clause in `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.attachments` states observable behavior only. The clauses are "YAML reports only `Comment` attachments", "Each `#` comment is one attachment, including a comment following a mapping value", and "A `#` within quoted text or within the content of a block scalar belongs to the scalar". None names a library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. Any parser or scanner that produced the same attachments would satisfy the text, whether it was hand-written, built on a YAML library, or split into different helpers. The choice of implementation is therefore discretionary. There are no implementation roots and no acknowledgments, and no structural obligation needs implementation evidence. Whether tests cover the behavior is a separate question for the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The `test.yaml` case in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` covers every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.attachments`.

The input is `a: |\n  # literal\n# standalone\nb: '# literal' # real\nc: "# literal"\n`. The test asserts the exact list of `(kind, text)` pairs found across all items: `[(Comment, "# standalone"), (Comment, "# real")]`.

- **Each `#` comment is one attachment, reported as `Comment`.** The standalone `# standalone` comment is reported as one `Comment`.
- **A comment following a mapping value is an attachment.** `# real` follows the value `'# literal'` on the `b:` line and is reported as a `Comment`.
- **A `#` inside a block scalar belongs to the scalar.** `# literal` in the `a: |` block is not reported.
- **A `#` inside quoted text belongs to the scalar.** The single-quoted `'# literal'` and the double-quoted `"# literal"` are both not reported.
- **Only `Comment` attachments are reported.** The assertion compares the whole list, including kinds, so any extra attachment or any other kind would fail it.

The test carries a `{test}` reference to this requirement. The other YAML scalar forms, such as a folded `>` scalar, fall into the same input classes as the ones tested.
